# developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs — Guides — Extend

> 8 page(s) of developer.paypal.com documentation — Braintree — Docs — Guides under Extend. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Extend

- [Configuration](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/configuration/): The [incoming forward request](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/forward-api/forward) is simply the body of the incoming request to the Forward API.
- [Transformations](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/transformations/): Here is an example of a transformation which builds an authorization header based on a username and password passed in on the request:
- [Tokenization Support](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/tokenization-support/): Contact your Account Manager for more information or
- [Hyperwallet Integration](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/hyperwallet/): Note
- [Worldpay](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/worldpay/): Note Any data sent to us this way appear in our logs. Users should refrain from sending us sensitive data and customer PII.
- [Examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/examples/): The Forward API provides a number of functions that can be used to construct requests.
- [Cryptography](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/cryptography/): Contact your Account Manager for more information or
- [PGP Public Key](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/extend/forward-api/pgp-key/): You'll need to use our public key to encrypt secrets sent during communication with the Forward API team.
